source: Issue #165. The policy-quality lint and the simulated preflight state their limits here, and test/authorization-lint.test.ts pins this list exactly. Narrowing is not part of this issue's deliverable.

entries.summary: The lint inspects the synthesized Foundation and Platform policy statements for the two Infra deployment and runtime principals only (#195 removed the per-service roles); the legacy pipeline role and CDK-generated service roles are outside its scope.
entries.consequence: A wildcard grant added to an unscanned role is caught only by review, not by the check.

entries.summary: The lint fails on wildcard actions, wildcard resource ARNs (including scoped ARNs such as stack or prefix forms), unreviewed managed-policy attachments and the repository's condition expectations. It evaluates statement text, not effective permission or condition values.
entries.consequence: The lint evaluates statement text; the simulator checks the plan's ARNs and the deployment itself exercises the real resource.

entries.summary: The CDK bootstrap cfn-exec role holds AdministratorAccess and no permissions boundary; no repository defines it. It is carried as a stated exception in the reviewed suppression table, not as a construct the lint can inspect.
entries.consequence: Effective permission on the Infra deploy path remains account-wide; the exception is recorded rather than asserted.

entries.summary: Since #195 the Runtime stack is synthesized by this repository (deployScope=runtime), so its template identity (AnyWearRuntimeStack) is covered by the matrix; the lint still scans only the Foundation and Platform policy documents, so a Runtime-template resource whose CloudFormation reads are ungranted stays outside the statement scan.
entries.consequence: A Runtime template type whose CloudFormation reads are ungranted is caught by the deployment itself or by an optional review, not by the Infra lint.

entries.summary: IAM policy simulation evaluates policies approximately: condition keys, resource policies, SCPs, permissions boundaries and service-specific semantics may differ from the real service.
entries.consequence: The preflight is a strong pre-mutation signal, not ground truth; the deployment's own behavior remains the final check.

entries.summary: The preflight simulates the Infra deploy and runtime roles only. The Runtime stack's CloudFormation execution role is the CDK bootstrap cfn-exec role (standard synthesizer, #195), which holds AdministratorAccess and no permissions boundary; it cannot be assumed or simulated from this job and is a stated lint exception.
entries.consequence: Those reads are covered by the statement lint and the deployment itself, not by the preflight.

entries.summary: The preflight evaluates policy against the reviewed ARNs in its plan; it does not sample live resources or make the real read calls. Mutations, waiter semantics, operator-CLI reads and the conditional CloudFront fallback are recorded as skips with reasons.
entries.consequence: Create-path authorization, resource existence and the real service semantics stay with the deployment itself.

entries.summary: iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy can enumerate any principal's effective permissions in the account. The grant is `*` because the simulator actions have no resource-level scope; it is limited to the two simulate actions, runs only in the restricted deploy/runtime session, and is used only by the preflight.
entries.consequence: The grant is read-only but is a permission-metadata disclosure surface; it is recorded here as an accepted reviewed wildcard.

entries.summary: Narrowing declared actions from actual usage is not part of this issue's deliverable.
entries.consequence: It remains an optional operator review, for example with IAM Access Analyzer or by manual analysis, under its own reviewed change; nothing here revokes a grant automatically.
